title: SF3661 (2025-2026 Regular): Prohibit the sale and possession of ghost guns

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (1st Engrossment, 2026-03-18; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/94/2026/0/SF/3661/versions/1/)
provenance.note: 1st Engrossment, 2026-03-18 (other). No vote in the record. Repeals Minn. Stat. 609.667 (the old serial-number offence) and replaces it in section 624.7145. Section 4 is a repealer.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7145, subd. 3): Any person who owns, possesses, or receives a ghost gun may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7145, subd. 4): Any person who sells, transfers, or distributes a ghost gun may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $10,000, or both.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7146, subd. 2): A person who is not a federal firearms licensee is prohibited from assembling or manufacturing more than three firearms in a calendar year.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7146, subd. 3): It is unlawful for a person, other than a federal firearms licensee, to manufacture a firearm using a computer numerical control milling machine or three-dimensional printer.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7146, subd. 4): It is unlawful to sell, transfer, or distribute to a person in the state, other than to a federal firearms licensee, digital instructions in the form of computer-aided design files or other code or instructions stored and displayed in electronic format as a digital model that may be used to program a three-dimensional printer to manufacture a ghost gun.
